To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The single-flash scheme is more efficient in terms of energy consumption and less expensive than the double-flash scheme; (2) The double-flash scheme results competitive only in the presence of stringent constraints on the methane slip; (3) The Pareto front highlights how the energy consumption and capital cost are conflicting objectives, i.e. a reduction of the energy consumption leads to an increase of the capital costs, and vice versa.

the single-flash water scrubbing process is superior in terms of capital costs and energy consumption to the double-flash process, and that the trade-off between capital costs and energy loss can be exploited to identify the most appropriate process design.

the single-flash configuration is the best choice for upgrading biogases from AD of agricultural residues to natural gas quality, and that the trade-off between capital costs and energy consumption of the water scrubber is very high, with the energy consumption increasing by 27 % when moving from the cheapest to the most efficient solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for the bi-objective optimization and design of a water scrubbing process.
the optimization of the water gasification process for biogases purification, with a focus on the techno-economic multi-objective optimization.
the techno-economic optimization of the water-scrubbing process for biomethane production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the double-flash scheme is more suitable to produce biomethane with a high purity level (methane slip < 0.5 %), while the single-flash scheme has the potential to be more competitive in the case of a low purity level (methan slip > 0.5%).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the single-flash configuration is the most cost-efficient solution when high methane slip is allowed.
the double flash scheme should be used if methane slip is limited, while the single flash scheme is the most suitable if methane slip can be high.

the single-flash configuration is the most suitable for biogas scrubbing when the energy consumption is the only criterion, while the double-flash scheme is the most suitable when both the methane slip and the energy loss are taken into account.
The main takeaway from our work is that

bi-objective optimization can be a valuable tool to assess the trade-off between the energy consumption and the capital cost of the water scrubber, and to support the selection of the best configuration of a process.
the water scrubbing biogas upgrading process is very sensitive to the methane slip and the capital costs are strongly dependent on the process design variables.
, for a given application, the optimization of the process design variables must take into account both energy consumption and capital cost.
